Here are the three findings from `app.log`:

## (1) First real error burst — time & host

| Event | Timestamp | Host |
|---|---|---|
| Batch job started, hoarding all connections | `2026-01-18T03:15:03Z` | `batch-01` |
| First db-pool error (the burst) | **`03:17:42Z`** | **`api-07`** — `db pool exhausted (max=20) waiting=14 path=/v1/orders` |
| Cascading to api-03, api-08, api-04, … | `03:17:43Z` | all api-* hosts |
| Last error in the burst | `03:19:22Z` | (api-05) |

The single TLS/handshake error at `02:41:07Z` on `api-02` is **unrelated noise** — a transient network glitch, not part of the outage.

## (2) Root cause

**Database connection pool exhaustion.** The primary DB pool has 20 connections. The batch job acquired all 20 and held them for ~26 minutes without releasing any:

```
03:15:03Z batch-01 job reconcile-ledger started user=svc-batch db_conns=20
03:15:04Z ... connection 1/20 from pool=primary
           ... (monotonically to 20/20 by 03:16:39Z)
03:41:30Z batch-01 job reconcile-ledger finished rows=48210112 released_conns=20
```

With every connection held, the API nodes had **zero** database connections available — all subsequent writes and queries failed with 503.

## (3) Responsible entity

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Host | `batch-01` |
| Job | **`reconcile-ledger`** |
| User / service account | **`svc-batch`** |
| Rows processed | 48,210,112 (held all 20 DB connections for the entire duration) |

The `reconcile-ledger` batch job grabbed the full pool upfront (`db_conns=20`) and held it until completion. A fix would be to split it into smaller chunks with connection release between batches, or give the batch job its own dedicated pool separate from the API nodes.
